mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically precedes a slowdown in economic growth and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the UNRATE increased by more than 0.3 percentage points in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST showed a sustained increase over the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month indicates a contraction in supply, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in the last month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2 percentage points in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months indicates strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS showed a consistent increase over the previous three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is above 3% in the last quarter, it signals a low-interest rate environment with strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and GDPC1 growth > 3% in 1 quarter
regime_hint: low-interest rate with strong economic growth
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was below 2% and GDPC1 growth was above 3% in the previous quarter.
